the most prevalent recurrent mutations are BRCA1 c.68-7_68delT, BRCA1 c.*2T>C, and BRCA2 IVS15-2A>G, which together comprise more than 50% of all BRAC mutations in the country.
1.4-1.5% of Lithuanian women are BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation carriers.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations in Lithuania was 8.2%, which is comparable to the prevalence of these gene alterations in other countries.
the BRCA1 and the BRCA2 genes in Lithuanians harbor a similar mutational spectrum as in other European populations.
in Lithuanian population BRCA1 mutations are more prevalent than BRCA2 mutations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the comprehensive BRCA1/BRCA2 mutational analysis should be recommended for all Lithuanian breast and ovarian cancer patients, regardless of the family history.
BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation analysis should be performed for all women with breast cancer or ovarian cancer in Lithuania.
